views.label: All
views.note: One Expo binary, the system browser for OIDC, the backend API as the authority, and two platform stores: the keystore and the local store.

views.label: Auth
views.note: OIDC + PKCE in the system browser, the code exchanged at the API, and the tokens written to the OS keystore behind the SecretStore port.

views.label: Offline
views.note: The outbox queue lives in the typed local store, drains on reconnect, foreground and a background task, and the server wins every conflict.

views.label: Push
views.note: Device tokens register on login and are revoked on logout; the tap uses the deep-link parser and carries no action of its own.

boundaries.label: The app binary — one variant, one bundle (APP_VARIANT)
Credential boundary — tokens live here and nowhere else
Local state — the only persistence the app owns

cards.title: The layer contract inside the binary
items: View → ViewModel → SDK → API: the View renders and forwards events, the ViewModel owns presentation state and commands, the SDK is a plain typed client, the API is the authority
the View never talks to the network — no fetch, no @/sdk import in a screen; the ViewModel is platform-free (no react-native, no react-dom, no views); the SDK never imports React or React Native
every screen renders every state — loading, empty, error, forbidden, offline, ready; a screen that renders a spinner for a lost connection is a broken contract, not a style choice

cards.title: One variant, one binary
items: APP_VARIANT picks game, market or avatar — separate bundle IDs, permissions and store listings; a combined super-app is not recommended
a variant that does not ship a feature does not bundle its native module or its assets: a market app must not carry a game engine
the app shell is React Native and heavy 3D is a replaceable module behind a SceneEngine port — auth, onboarding, settings, push and the market flows never depend on an engine

cards.title: The client is untrusted
items: game state, prices, payments and entitlements are server-authoritative; the client shapes UX and never decides access
the deep link and the push payload are untrusted input: parse against the route allowlist, validate every parameter, and offer an action instead of performing one
jailbreak or root is a server-side risk signal, never a client-side block; certificate pinning only ships with a rotation plan

cards.title: The contract is machine-checkable
items: lints/eslint.config.mjs pins the walls with no-restricted-imports per path: views deny @/sdk, viewmodels deny react-native/react-dom/@/views, the SDK denies react/react-native/@/session

lints/check/ is the violation harness — one deliberate file per rule with an // expect:<rule> marker plus a clean control; scripts/check-lints.sh fails if a marked rule stays quiet, if anything unmarked fires, or if tsc --noEmit fails
a config exception is a contract change: when a change would cross a layer, re-cut the layout instead of adding a path to the exception list
